newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's H-shares surge, investors rotate.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's H-shares surge, investors rotate.

text.p: Shares of mainland Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong surged on Thursday, benefiting from rotational buying as investors found the H-shares more attractive than the blue-chip sector, analysts said.
The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index hit a day high of 1,043.68 before closing at 1,032.49, up 29.90 points, or 2.98 percent, on active buying.
It outperformed the Hang Seng blue-chip index, which rose 4.77 points, or 0.04 percent, to 13,546.60.
"Blue chips look weak. Investors are selectively buying red chips and now people are buying H-shares," an analyst at a Japanese house said.
One broker said investors were also picking up laggards.
Maanshan Iron rose HK$0.06 to HK$1.78 and Guangzhou Shipyard gained HK$0.13 to HK$1.97.
Luoyang Glass jumped HK$0.05 to HK$1.69 and Shanghai Petrochemical was up HK$0.125 at HK$2.20.
The analysts said the market had already discounted disappointing 1996 results due to be reported in late March and April and that H-shares were expected to continue moving higher.
